title: "Company" or "Co."? Worker alleges one abbreviation hid a live policy - Insurance Business
content:
What happened: A Texas worker alleges her insurer created a shadow claim by changing one word in a database entry, hiding a live workers’ comp policy while denying her benefits for 17 months. Who’s involved: ACE American Insurance Company (Chubb subsidiary), ESIS (claims administrator), CITGO Petroleum Corporation (employer), MediCall/Cognizant, Texas state agencies. What’s at stake: Approximately $110,000 per year in indemnity benefits allegedly diverted for over 17 months, plus triple damages under civil RICO. Why it matters: The complaint describes a specific alleged exploit in the TXCOMP workers’ comp database that claims professionals and carrier IT teams will want to understand. Where it stands: Emergency complaint with TRO motion filed October 15, 2026; no court ruling yet. "Company" or "Co."? One worker alleges that single abbreviation was enough to split her workers' compensation claim in two - one that paid out behind the scenes, and one that denied her everything. A former CITGO Petroleum Corporation employee has filed a 59-page emergency complaint in US District Court for the Western District of Texas, alleging that ACE American Insurance Company - a subsidiary of Chubb - and its claims administrator ESIS ran what the filing calls a parallel "dual-claim" operation inside the state's workers' compensation database for more than 17 months. The complaint zeroes in on how the Texas workers' comp database, known as TXCOMP, identifies insurance carriers. Rather than using a fixed federal identification number, the filing says, the system relies on text-based combinations of the claimant's name, employer name, and carrier name. According to the complaint, the defendants took advantage of that design by maintaining two separate carrier entries: "ACE American Insurance Company" on one, and "ACE American Insurance Co." on the other. The difference between "Company" and "Co." allegedly created two entirely separate data tracks for a single workplace injury, the complaint states. The filing calls the first track (DWC No. 25169058) a "Secret Financial Revenue Engine" - allegedly registered on the backend as a live, approved, and active policy tied to the plaintiff's true identity and an approximately $110,000 annual salary. The second track (DWC No. 25183607), created roughly 35 days later, is described in the filing as an "External Consumer Deflector" - a permanently denied record that blocked the plaintiff from accessing income benefits, medical care, and a prescribed wheelchair. The employer name was also allegedly split: "CITGO Petroleum Corporation" on one track, "CITGO Petroleum Corp." on the other. One of the more striking sections of the complaint deals with a $250 physical therapy evaluation. According to the filing, when the plaintiff requested approval for emergency cardiac care, the claims adjuster "issued blanket denials within minutes via informal email channels." But when the $250 evaluation was submitted, the complaint says the adjuster retained MediCall - a medical management arm of Fortune 500 company Cognizant - to conduct a formal utilization review, which is a regulated process where a carrier brings in an outside medical reviewer to approve or deny a treatment request. The complaint frames this as a telling contradiction. The filing argues that under Texas insurance law, a carrier has no legal basis to order a utilization review on a claim it says is dead and closed. The fact that it did, the complaint says, amounts to "an irrefutable admission by conduct" that the underlying policy was still live. According to the filing, the plaintiff had already completed roughly 80% of the evaluation when the review kicked in. The complaint says the plaintiff collapsed after trying to lift a 10-pound weight - about the heft of a gallon of milk - during the assessment. Rather than treating the collapse as proof of disability, the filing alleges the insurer used the incident to pressure the clinic into withholding the final evaluation report. That report, the complaint says, was needed to complete a federal disability benefits application. The complaint lays out a detailed electronic timeline that the filing says reveals the hidden backend activity. According to the complaint, in February and March 2026, independent providers ran billing through the original claim number and received automated confirmations of an active, funded workers' comp policy. The filing alleges these electronic responses returned specific database details including the employer's guarantor ID, the carrier claim number as subscriber ID, and the plaintiff's date of birth - all consistent with a live policy. On March 13, 2026, the complaint states, the system cleared and approved the plaintiff's prescribed NuMotion custom wheelchair (a TiliteAeroX with Motor SmartDrive). A technician verbally confirmed the approval four days later, according to the filing. The complaint alleges the claims adjuster then manually overrode the system to block delivery. The filing also alleges that before a high-risk nuclear cardiac stress test, someone swapped the plaintiff's real emergency contact number for an unauthorized phone number in her cardiologist's patient records. The complaint calls this "a lethal mechanism" - arguing that a cardiac emergency during the test would have routed notifications to the wrong person. The 10-count complaint includes allegations of civil racketeering (RICO), healthcare fraud, computer fraud, and violations of the Texas Labor Code. The filing seeks an emergency court order to reinstate income benefits going back to their start date, delivery of the wheelchair, and triple damages on all diverted funds. The complaint also says the plaintiff faces losing a home with approximately $670,000 in equity and is currently surviving on $298 per month in food assistance. Two state agencies - TDI-DWC and OIEC - are named as defendants, with the filing alleging they left the plaintiff's medical condition to deteriorate untreated. If the allegations prove out, the case could sharpen scrutiny on how state workers' compensation databases verify carrier identities - and whether text-based matching creates openings for the kind of parallel-claim scheme described in this filing. The allegations in the complaint have not been tested, and no court has ruled on the merits. (NYSE:MRK) have something important in common that is important for investors, which is that both must demonstrate that newer medicines can sustain earnings as their established blockbusters face competition. However, the companies are at different stages of that transition, creating an interesting valuation dilemma. According to Yahoo Finance’s valuation snapshot, AbbVie trades at 16.39 times forward earnings, compared with 15.29 times for Merck. That represents a relatively modest premium for AbbVie, despite a considerable difference in recent revenue growth. For investors, the question is whether AbbVie’s stronger current performance makes it the more attractive investment, or whether Merck offers greater potential as its newer products expand. AbbVie Inc. (NYSE:ABBV) has already demonstrated that its growth strategy can deliver results beyond Humira. Second-quarter revenue increased 10.2% on a reported basis to $16.99 billion, while adjusted earnings per share climbed 22.9% to $3.65. Skyrizi and Rinvoq remain central to that performance. The two immunology medicines generated approximately $8.03 billion in combined quarterly revenue, representing a considerable chunk of total sales for the company. Global Skyrizi net revenue increased 24.4% on a reported basis, while Rinvoq grew 24.5%. These figures are particularly important for investors because AbbVie is generating substantial replacement revenue while Humira sales continue declining. That gives investors evidence of an established commercial transition rather than relying entirely on future drug launches. Read more extensively about AbbVie’s bull and bear case here. Merck’s growth, on the other hand, has been more moderate. Total worldwide sales in fiscal Q2 2026 increased 5% to $16.6 billion, with Keytruda and Keytruda Qlex generating approximately $8.4 billion, also up 5%. However, Merck has promising growth opportunities outside its leading oncology franchise. Winrevair revenue increased 75% to $588 million, while the company’s Animal Health business sales grew 8% to $1.8 billion. Merck’s expanding portfolio could gradually reduce its dependence on Keytruda. If newer medicines deliver meaningful revenue contributions, investors could become more confident in its ability to sustain earnings beyond its current blockbuster franchise. The distinction between the two companies becomes more significant when considering revenue concentration. Although AbbVie has successfully expanded Skyrizi and Rinvoq, their combined contribution of nearly half of quarterly revenue creates substantial dependence on continued immunology growth. Any meaningful slowdown in these products would challenge the earnings expectations supporting its valuation. Merck & Co., Inc. (NYSE:MRK) faces a different problem, with Keytruda and Keytruda Qlex accounting for approximately 50% of second-quarter revenue. With Keytruda’s U.S. loss of exclusivity approaching in 2028, the company must build enough additional revenue to offset potential future pressure on its largest franchise. There is also uncertainty around how quickly newer medicines can bridge that gap. Winrevair’s rapid growth is encouraging, but its $588 million quarterly contribution remains relatively small compared with Keytruda’s $8.4 billion. Merck, however, presents an interesting alternative. Its emerging medicines offer opportunities to diversify revenue, although their ability to compensate for future Keytruda competition remains uncertain. The valuation difference is small enough that investors should focus less on the headline P/E and more on earnings durability. AbbVie offers greater visibility into an already advancing growth transition, while Merck’s investment case depends more heavily on the commercial success of its next generation of medicines. Ultimately, AbbVie may be able to justify its premium through continued execution. Merck & Co., Inc. title: Weekly Buzz: RHHBY, TEVA Win FDA Nod; MLAB, GSK Cut Jobs; AZN, VIR Deals; KRYS, ABBV Report Data - RTTNews
content: This week's healthcare roundup brings a series of regulatory wins, corporate restructuring, billion-dollar deals and clinical milestones. Roche and Teva gained FDA approvals, while Mesa Laboratories and GSK moved ahead with workforce cuts. Strategic moves also took center stage, with Labcorp, AstraZeneca, Galderma and Zealand Pharma announcing notable acquisitions and collaborations. Clinical updates added further momentum, with companies reporting promising findings in several disease areas alongside trial setbacks that could reshape development plans. Let us unpack this week's key healthcare developments. Roche Expands Enspryng's Reach with FDA Approval for Thyroid Eye Disease Roche Holding AG (RHHBY) received FDA approval for Enspryng (satralizumab) to treat adults with thyroid eye disease (TED), introducing the first at-home subcutaneous treatment option for the condition. Approval was supported by Phase 3 SatraGo studies, with SatraGO-2 showing improved eye bulging response (52.9% vs. 23.4%) and double vision (60.7% vs. 25.8%) versus placebo. Enspryng was previously approved for neuromyelitis optical spectrum disorder (NMOSD). RHHBY closed Thursday's trading (October 15, 2026) at $56.78, up 1.96% Foresee's CAMCEVI Wins China Approval for Advanced Prostate Cancer Foresee Pharmaceuticals (6576.TWO) received approval from China's NMPA for CAMCEVI 42 mg to treat adults with advanced prostate cancer. The six-month subcutaneous leuprolide formulation will be commercialized by licensing partner GenSci, expanding CAMCEVI's global reach; a separate application for premenopausal breast cancer remains under review in China. 6576.TWO closed Friday's trading at TWD 77.60, up 0.52% Asahi Kasei Scores FDA Approval for First-in-Class HSV Treatment Asahi Kasei Corp. (AHKSF) received FDA approval for HOVILPRI (pritelivir), a first-in-class therapy for drug-resistant or treatment-refractory herpes simplex virus (HSV) lesions in immunocompromised adults. Approval was supported by Phase 3 PRIOH-1 Part C trial, which demonstrated superiority over existing therapies, addressing a critical unmet medical need. Teva Wins FDA Nod for Once-Monthly Schizophrenia Treatment Teva Pharmaceuticals (TEVA) received FDA approval for WELTRUZA (olanzapine), the first once-monthly subcutaneous long-acting injectable formulation of olanzapine for adults with schizophrenia. Approval was supported by the Phase 3 SOLARIS trial data showing improvements in symptoms, illness severity, and social functioning, with no post-injection monitoring required. TEVA closed Thursday's trading at $41.11, up 0.96% Mesa Laboratories to Lay Off 40 Employees in Global Restructuring Mesa Laboratories, Inc. (MLAB) plans to cut approximately 40 jobs, representing 6% of its global workforce, primarily in its Clinical Genomics division, as part of a restructuring program. The company expects the plan, which also includes facility footprint reductions and lower third-party spending, to generate approximately $9.3 million in annualized cost savings. MLAB closed Thursday's trading at $127.74, up 1.25% GSK Restructuring Plan Puts 1,217 Belgian Jobs at Risk GSK plc (GSK) faces close monitoring by Belgian authorities over its restructuring plan, which could affect 1,217 jobs in the country. Belgium's Deputy Prime Minister David Clarinval stressed that the company must comply with labor laws and ensure proper employee consultation during the process. Labcorp To Acquire Select BioReference Assets From OPKO In Deal Worth Up To $872 Million Labcorp (LH) will acquire select BioReference Health assets from OPKO Health (OPK), including its diagnostic testing businesses, 80+ patient service centers, and the 4Kscore prostate cancer test, in a deal valued at up to $872 million. OPKO will receive $722 million in cash upfront and may earn up to $150 million in additional milestone payments tied to future 4Kscore revenue. Labcorp expects the acquired businesses to generate approximately $250 million in revenue during the first year after closing, based on its current forecasts. Insitro, AstraZeneca Partner To Develop AI-Discovered MASH and Cardiomyopathy Therapies Insitro has entered into a worldwide exclusive research collaboration with AstraZeneca (AZN) to discover novel drug targets and therapies for metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH) and cardiomyopathies. Insitro will use its AI-powered Virtual Human platform to identify disease targets for AstraZeneca and advance them through discovery, while AstraZeneca will lead clinical development and commercialisation. Insitro will receive $40 million upfront and is eligible for up to $1.46 billion in milestone payments, plus single-digit royalties on future global sales. Adlai Nortye Partners With Lilly And Merck KGaA To Evaluate AN4035 Adlai Nortye Group (ANL) has partnered with Eli Lilly (LLY) and Merck KGaA (MRK.DE) to evaluate its cancer therapy AN4035 in combination with cetuximab (ERBITUX). Lilly will supply cetuximab for the US, and Merck will supply cetuximab for the Australian and Chinese trial sites, while Adlai Nortye remains the study sponsor. AN4035, an anti-RAS (ON) inhibitor-based ADC, will be evaluated as monotherapy and in combination with cetuximab in the ongoing global Phase I trial and the collaboration is based on the scientific rationale of simultaneously targeting EGFR and RAS signalling pathways, a strategy researchers believe could benefit RAS-driven cancers. Vir Biotechnology Partners With Gilead On Next-Generation Cancer Immunotherapy Programs Vir Biotechnology, Inc. (VIR) has entered into a multi-program collaboration and license agreement with Gilead Sciences (GILD) to discover and develop three novel PRO-XTEN dual-masked T-cell engager (TCE) development candidates targeting selected solid tumour-associated antigens. Under the agreement, Gilead will receive exclusive rights to develop and commercialise the resulting therapies. Vir could receive up to $1.88 billion under the deal, including $135 million in upfront and near-term payments, up to $1.74 billion in future milestones, and tiered royalties on potential product sales. Sangamo Plans ST-503 Auction by Q4 2026 Amid Chapter 11 Proceedings Sangamo Therapeutics (SGMOQ) plans to auction its ST-503 gene therapy program for small fibre neuropathy-associated pain by Q4 2026 as part of its Chapter 11 asset sales. The company has already sold ST-920 to PTC Therapeutics and ST-506 to Eli Lilly (LLY) for a combined $163.55 million, while ST-503 remains in Phase 1/2 development. Galderma to Acquire ZO Skin Health for $1.5 Billion Galderma (GALD.SW) signed an agreement to acquire ZO Skin Health for $1.5 billion in an all-cash deal, expanding its dermatological skincare portfolio alongside Cetaphil and Alastin. The acquisition is expected to close in Q4 2026 or early 2027, subject to customary conditions, and ZO Skin Health reported approximately $330 million in sales over the 12 months ended June 2026. GALD.SW closed Thursday's trade at 172.15 Swiss Francs. Zealand Pharma, Generate Biomedicines Ink $1.2 Billion AI Drug Discovery Deal Zealand Pharma (ZEAL.CO) partnered with Generate Biomedicines (GENB) to develop AI-designed protein therapies for obesity and other metabolic diseases, initially covering two programs with an option for a third. Generate will receive $30 million upfront and up to $35 million in early preclinical milestones, with nearly $1.2 billion in potential development, regulatory and commercial milestones, plus tiered royalties. ZEAL.CO closed Thursday's trade at 229.90 Danish Kroner, up 0.22% Roche Licenses Rona's RNAi Obesity Candidate in $1.16 Billion Deal Roche (RHHBY) entered a global licensing agreement with Rona Therapeutics for an investigational RNAi therapy targeting ALK7 to treat obesity and metabolic disease. Rona is eligible to receive up to $100 million in upfront and near-term milestones, up to $1.06 billion in additional development, regulatory and commercial milestones, plus tiered royalties on future sales. RHHBY closed Thursday's trade at $56.78, up 1.96%. Prelude Therapeutics, Lilly Partner To Evaluate PRT13722 In Breast Cancer Trial Prelude Therapeutics Inc. (PRLD) has entered into a clinical trial collaboration and supply agreement with Eli Lilly and Company (LLY) to evaluate PRT13722, an oral KAT6A selective degrader, in combination with Verzenio (abemaciclib), a CDK4/6 inhibitor, and Inluriyo (imlunestrant), an oral estrogen receptor antagonist in patients with HR+/HER2- breast cancer. Under the agreement, Lilly will supply Verzenio and Inluriyo for use in Prelude's Phase 1 study and the combination cohorts will evaluate PRT13722 alongside these established breast cancer therapies. For Prelude, the agreement provides an opportunity to evaluate whether combining PRT13722 with established breast cancer treatments can further improve outcomes for patients with HR+/HER2-disease Stryker, CMR Surgical Form Strategic Alliance To Advance Robotic-Assisted Surgery Stryker Corp. (SYK) announced a strategic equity investment of approximately $400 million with an exclusive option to acquire the remaining equity of CMR Surgical and an exclusive U.S. commercial agency agreement for the Versius portfolio, a next-generation surgical robot. The agreement combines CMR Surgical's soft-tissue robotics portfolio and clinical experience with Stryker's commercial capabilities, customer relationships and global market presence. Stryker will serve as the exclusive U.S. sales agent for the Versius portfolio, while CMR Surgical will continue to lead portfolio development and commercialisation in markets outside the United States. Krystal Biotech Reports Over 80% Lesion Regression With KB113 In Gorlin Syndrome Krystal Biotech, Inc. (KRYS) announced positive preliminary clinical data for KB113, an investigational intratumoral immunotherapy being developed to treat basal cell carcinomas (BCCs) in patients with Gorlin syndrome, a rare genetic condition. In a pilot study of three adult patients, KB113 induced clinical regression in more than 80% of evaluated lesions, with responses seen in both injected and non-injected lesions. Biopsies confirmed complete tumor clearance in one injected lesion per patient. The treatment was well tolerated, with only mild-to-moderate, transient adverse events. Krystal is in discussions with the FDA on the next steps for KB113's clinical development in Gorlin syndrome. Galderma Reports Sustained Nemolizumab Benefits In Children With Atopic Dermatitis Galderma Group AG (GALD.SW) reported new Phase 2 data showing sustained improvements in itch, sleep disturbance, and quality of life through week 52 with nemolizumab, an investigational monoclonal antibody targeting IL-31 signalling in children aged 2-11 years with moderate-to-severe atopic dermatitis. Galderma said the treatment was well tolerated, with no new safety signals identified, and that the results remain consistent with the previously established clinical benefits of nemolizumab in patients with atopic dermatitis. GALD closed Thursday's trade at 172.15 Swiss francs. Arrowhead Reports Positive Phase 1/2a Data for ARO-MAPT in Alzheimer's Arrowhead Pharmaceuticals, Inc. (ARWR) announced positive interim results from an ongoing Phase 1/2a study of ARO-MAPT, the company's investigational RNA interference (RNAi) therapeutic for Alzheimer's disease and other tauopathies. According to the company, in healthy volunteers, subcutaneous ARO-MAPT administration achieved durable reductions in cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) total tau, with a mean reduction of up to 73% at day 105 and a maximum reduction of 85%, supporting the potential for once-quarterly dosing. ARO-MAPT was generally well tolerated. Most treatment-emergent adverse events (TEAEs) were grade 1 or mild. Entrada Reports Positive Cohort 1 Data for ENTR-601-45 Entrada Therapeutics (TRDA) announced Cohort 1 of the Phase 1/2 ELEVATE-45-201 study of ENTR-601-45 met its primary endpoint of safety and tolerability at the initial 5 mg/kg dose in ambulatory patients with Duchenne muscular dystrophy (DMD) amenable to exon 45 skipping. Secondary analyses showed a mean 0.10% increase in dystrophin production from baseline. The company also reported that enrollment in Cohort 2 is complete, with data from the 10 mg/kg dose cohort expected in the first half of 2027. Biomea Reports Weight-Loss Data For Oral GLP-1 Candidate BMF-650 Biomea Fusion Inc. (BMEA) reported Phase 1 results for BMF-650, its investigational oral glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) receptor agonist for obesity and metabolic disorders. According to the company, mean weight reduction ranged from 1.5% to 3.2% at day 29 across Cohorts 1-4, compared with 0.1% for pooled placebo, with no severe treatment-related adverse events. A one-step titration to 400 mg once daily was well tolerated in Cohort 5, with mild TEAEs; nausea and vomiting were reported in 12.5% of participants, supporting further evaluation of no-titration dosing. AbbVie Reports 35.8% Endoscopic Remission With Subcutaneous Skyrizi In Crohn's Trial AbbVie Inc. (ABBV) presented new positive Phase 3 AFFIRM trial data showing endoscopic remission and ulcer-free endoscopy outcomes with subcutaneous Skyrizi, an interleukin-23 (IL-23) inhibitor in adults with active Crohn's disease. According to the company, the data showed that at week 24, endoscopic remission reached 35.8% with Skyrizi, compared with 9.1% with placebo. Ulcer-free endoscopy was reported in 36.6% versus 9.1%, respectively. Skyrizi is currently approved for Crohn's disease with intravenous induction and subcutaneous maintenance therapy, while a fully subcutaneous induction regimen is under review by the FDA and EMA. ABBV closed Thursday's trade at $283.40, up 0.59%. BioNTech's BNT113 Fails PFS Goal in Phase 3 Trial, OS Assessment Continues BioNTech SE (BNTX) announced that its AHEAD-MERIT Phase 2/3 trial evaluating BNT113, an investigational mRNA cancer immunotherapy in combination with pembrolizumab, did not meet the primary endpoint of progression-free survival (PFS) compared with pembrolizumab alone in patients with HPV16-positive head and neck cancer. However, the Independent Data Monitoring Committee recommended continuing the study to assess overall survival. Under the trial's prespecified statistical design, a statistically significant improvement in OS could establish a positive trial outcome despite the PFS result. BNTX closed Thursday's trading at $90.20, up 1.74%. Syndax's Phase 2 MAXPIRe Trial Of Axatilimab Misses Primary Endpoint In IPF Syndax Pharmaceuticals Inc. (SNDX) announced that the MAXPIRe Phase 2 trial of axatilimab, an investigational monoclonal antibody in idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF), did not meet its primary endpoint of the annualized rate of decline in forced vital capacity (FVC). Based on these results, Syndax does not plan to pursue further development of axatilimab in IPF, but the company will continue to evaluate axatilimab in frontline chronic graft-versus-host disease trials, with data expected later in 2026. J&J Reports Up To 94% Clinical Remission With Tremfya In 3-Year Crohn's Data Johnson & Johnson (JNJ) reported new three-year data from the Phase 3 GALAXI 2 and GALAXI 3 long-term extension (LTE) studies showing sustained clinical and endoscopic remission with Tremfya, a monoclonal antibody in adults with active Crohn's disease. According to the company, the new key findings included that at week 144, clinical remission rates were 94% with the 100 mg regimen and 91% with the 200 mg regimen. Both groups achieved an 88% 90-day corticosteroid-free clinical remission rate with safety findings consistent with Tremfya's in Crohn's disease. JNJ closed Thursday's trade at $253.28, down 0.25%. Bristol Myers Reports Positive Phase 3 Admilparant Data in IPF Bristol Myers Squibb (BMY) announced positive topline results from its pivotal Phase 3 ALOFT-IPF trial, evaluating admilparant, an investigational oral therapy that met the study's primary endpoint in adults with idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis. According to the company, the study met its primary endpoint at the 60 mg dose, with patients receiving admilparant demonstrating a statistically significant improvement in the change in forced vital capacity (FVC) from baseline at Week 52, a key measure of lung function, compared with placebo. At the 120 mg dose, admilparant also slowed the decline in lung function, although the result did not reach statistical significance. Bristol Myers will review the full Phase 3 data and consult regulators on potential submissions. Mirum Pharmaceuticals Reports Positive Phase 3 LIVMARLI Results Mirum Pharmaceuticals, Inc. (MIRM), announced that the Phase 3 EXPAND study of LIVMARLI (maralixibat), an orally administered ileal bile acid transporter (IBAT) inhibitor, was conducted in patients with ultra-rare cholestatic liver diseases. According to the company, in the pediatric population, maralixibat produced a mean 1.81-point improvement in the ItchRO(Obs) severity score during weeks 13-20, compared with a 0.83-point improvement for placebo. The placebo-adjusted treatment difference was 0.98 points (p=0.0004). Mirum plans to submit a supplemental New Drug Application (sNDA) to the U.S. Food and Drug Administration in the first half of 2027.
